changes.summary: Owner cards on the Owners page were wearing decade-old logos. Eight owners — Dangsters, Ninjas, Midwestside, Pigskins, Wabbits, Bring The Pain, Dark Magicians, Fire Ready Aim — now show the logo they actually run today instead of the one they retired years ago.

Owner cards on the Owners page now show your current team, not your longest-running one. Shawn Huber gets Suh girls, one cup instead of a logo he retired in 2018, and Shawn Klezovich finally gets the Swiftie spelling. Last-place rebrands still don't count — Ross Lawrence keeps the Thundering Herd.
The Owners page now leads with current owners — the "Champions you've never seen" callout moved below the card grid instead of sitting above it.
Music City Mafia's dark-mode logo no longer sits on a black box — the skyline backdrop is gone and the detective now floats clean on the page like every other team's icon.

The "Together" column on Strength of Division was counting seasons with the same four franchises, which isn't the same as the same four owners — the Southwest was credited with nine shared years for a group that's only been together since 2020. Together now means exactly what it says: seasons this group of owners has played together, restarting when a team changes hands. A new Founded column carries the division's own age, so a young lineup in an old division reads right.
